summary: Deploy safety tool pack, stdlib only and deliberately free: gating this makes free-tier output worse, and the tool that stops someone wiping their own .env is the tool that earns the upgrade. unit-lint.py reads a systemd unit against the filesystem it will run on and reports only what stops it starting — an ExecStart the deploy never rsynced or left non-executable, a WorkingDirectory that does not exist or that ProtectHome hides, an EnvironmentFile that is world-readable, a ReadWritePaths that does not cover where the app actually writes under ProtectSystem, a missing Restart or a 100ms RestartSec that burns the start limit, a relative path where systemd demands absolute, a Type=notify over a shell or interpreter that hangs 90 seconds and then fails, and a unit name that would silently replace an installed one. It is the half systemd-analyze verify cannot see, and every finding it prints is a twenty-minute edit-rsync-daemon-reload-journalctl loop that did not happen. smoke-check.py asserts what a deployed site actually serves rather than that something answered: per check a status, contains, not_contains, content-type, max latency and a minimum body size, and it is not_contains plus min_bytes that catch the failures a curl gate cannot — an incremental build that left a stale route directory behind, and an SPA shell served where content should be. Neither tool mutates anything: unit-lint writes nothing, smoke-check issues GET and HEAD only, and neither imports subprocess, because the repo is the source and a tool that fixes a unit in place edits the runtime instead.
